title: LightGBM native Booster ignores the serialization_format default
answers: lightgbm Booster logged with cloudpickle label
native lightgbm model serialization format on Databricks
lightgbm serialization_format not applied to Booster
body:
Invariant: a native lightgbm.Booster is always saved in LightGBM's native format; only non-Booster (sklearn-style) models use serialization_format.
Enforced in: mlflow/lightgbm/__init__.py:save_model, which branches on isinstance(lgb_model, lgb.Booster) before serializing.
What breaks if skipped: the Databricks-dependent default (_get_default_serialization_format) gets applied to Booster inputs, so the flavor configuration and logged-model telemetry report "cloudpickle" for a format that was never used. Reviewer comments flagged the helper as resolving without considering model type.
Constraints: Model-type check should gate the Databricks default; the helper alone does not check model type.
applies: LightGBM save_model/log_model and any code that reads serialization_format from the flavor configuration.
says: Logged native gradient boosted models display the wrong serialization format on the model page.
Model details screen shows pickle format label for native booster models logged in Databricks.
Experiment tracking view reports incorrect storage format for native gradient boosting models.
Saved native booster models should accurately reflect native format in model catalog metadata.
search: In mlflow/lightgbm/__init__.py:save_model, a native lightgbm.Booster is always saved in native format and must bypass serialization_format. Checking isinstance(lgb_model, lgb.Booster) gates the Databricks default from _get_default_serialization_format to prevent flavor configuration and telemetry from incorrectly reporting cloudpickle. Only non-Booster models use serialization_format because _get_default_serialization_format does not inspect model type.
